mods.name: Create Optimized Trains
mods.description:
Performance optimization addon for Create Mod trains.
Includes LOD rendering, carriage grouping, safe multi-threading,
tick throttling, render optimization, proxy entities,
smart chunk management, physics & networking optimization,
priority system and dynamic performance monitor.

releases.notes:
## v1.4.0

### Focus

- Fixes leaked force-loaded chunks (#8), server lag from synchronous chunk loading, and slow chunk loading for players on foot
- Adds an in-game **Performance Analyzer** to make reporting problems easy

### Bug Fixes

#### Leaked force-loaded chunks (#8)
- The rate-limited unload loop removed *all* pending chunks from tracking, even the ones it had not released yet — those chunks stayed force-loaded forever with no owner, retaining thousands of ChunkHolders over time
- Fix: only chunks that were actually released are removed from tracking; the rest are released on the next ticks
- Chunks of trains that are removed or disassembled are now released too
- **Existing worlds:** older versions used vanilla `/forceload`, which is saved in the world. If you used v1.3.2 or older, run `/forceload remove all` once in each dimension (this also removes any forceloads you created yourself)

#### Chunk tickets
- Train chunks now use the mod's own region tickets instead of vanilla `/forceload`: they are not saved to the world, never conflict with player forceloads, and two trains in the same chunk no longer release it for each other

#### Server lag spikes while trains move
- Forcing a chunk loaded/generated it **synchronously** on the server thread (12–180 ms per train update). Chunks are now requested asynchronously

#### Slow chunk loading for players on foot
- Trains that had entities kept their chunks force-loaded wherever they went, so after a while every train on the map was loading chunks and the server tick had no spare time left for the player's chunks (pausing the game "fixed" it)
- Unoccupied trains far from every player (beyond `ghostDistance`, min. view distance + 4 chunks) now release their chunks and keep running on the track without entities

#### Multi-dimension trains
- Trains in the Nether or other dimensions were handled as if they were in the Overworld (chunks forced in the wrong dimension, wrong distances)

#### Leaving and re-entering a world
- All optimization systems were shut down on the first world exit and never restarted in singleplayer

#### Carriages appearing with stutter
- New carriages had movement interpolation disabled for 5 ticks, making them jump at 20 Hz when entering view; interpolation is now only skipped on real position corrections
- Stress immunity now also covers carriages that just appeared, so their alignment no longer stops the train

#### Other
- Collision checks between trains are no longer skipped at high speed (trains could pass through each other)
- Directional chunk loading no longer leaves permanent holes when you leave the train or it turns
- LOD is computed on the main thread only (it read non-thread-safe Create state)
- `chunks.maxChunkWaitTicks` now actually works
- The mod version shown in the mods list is now correct

### New Features

#### Performance Analyzer
- Open it from the Esc menu, from Mods → Create Optimized Trains → Config, or with a key (Options → Controls, unbound by default)
- Records FPS, frame times, server MSPT, trains, chunk loading and memory while you play (max 5 minutes), then saves a JSON report to `.minecraft/cot-reports/`
- One-click buttons to open the folder, copy the report to Downloads, open a pre-filled GitHub issue, or join the Discord
- No personal data is recorded (no name, UUID, IP, seed or coordinates)
- Server owners: `/cot profiler start | stop | discard | status` (operators only)

#### Create-style config screen
- The mod's config can now be edited in-game with the same screen as Create

#### Chunk prewarming
- Chunks entering the view of a player riding a train are loaded ahead of time, bypassing vanilla's limit of 4 player chunks at a time. New `prewarm` config section
- Never more than `prewarm.maxPending` (default 24) prewarmed chunks waiting to load/generate at once, and prewarming pauses while the server is lagging, so it can't flood world generation and stall the server tick

### Config

releases.notes:
# Changelog

## v1.3.2

### Focus

- Fixes the remaining Copycats+ bit lag, a critical world-load freeze, and last-carriage movement stutter
- All fixes are follow-ups discovered while stress-testing v1.3.1 on maps with 40+ trains and Copycats+ bit-heavy contraptions

### Bug Fixes

#### Copycats+ Periodic Lag (Bit Blocks with BlockEntity)
- Contraptions containing Copycats+ "bits" (sub-block sized pieces with a BlockEntity, unlike plain slabs/panels) caused periodic lag spikes every few seconds
- Root cause: `ContraptionWorld` does not override `getBlockEntity()`, so it fell back to `WrappedLevel.getBlockEntity()`, which queried the **real world** using the contraption's **local** coordinates (e.g. 5,1,3) — forcing the server to load/query the chunk at real-world (0,0) on every call
- Fix: `ContraptionWorldBlockEntityMixin` intercepts `getBlockEntity()` on `Level` (filtered to `ContraptionWorld` instances) and always serves the BlockEntity from `contraption.getBlocks()`, with a lazy per-instance cache — never touching the real world with local coordinates

#### World Freeze on Startup (Memory Pressure)
- On some world loads, especially after the server had been running a while, the game would hang completely at the loading screen (no crash, just a full freeze)
- Root cause: heap memory pressure genuinely reaching 90%+ during startup, mainly from Distant Horizons' distant world generation competing with ~40 Create contraptions being assembled simultaneously — triggering long stop-the-world GC pauses (minutes-long in the worst case)
- Fix: `DistantHorizonsThrottle` temporarily reduces DH's distant world generation and worker thread count for the first `startupThrottleTicks` (default 200 ticks / 10s) after the server starts, giving vanilla terrain and contraption assembly priority. DH's original settings are restored automatically afterwards. Uses DH's public API via reflection — no hard dependency

#### Last-Carriage Movement Stutter
- Long trains (10+ carriages) without a player on board showed irregular movement — the stutter would noticeably improve once the rearmost carriage's entity finally loaded
- Root cause: `ChunkLoadManager`'s per-tick chunk load rate limit applied to *every* needed chunk indiscriminately, including the exact chunk each carriage physically occupies. On unoccupied trains, that chunk competed with lookahead/trailing chunks for the same 6-per-tick budget, so the last carriage in line could take several ticks just to get its own chunk loaded — delaying its entity creation
- Fix: chunk requests are now split into **critical** (the exact chunk under each carriage — always loaded immediately, no rate limit, regardless of occupancy) and **soft** (LOD comfort radius, directional lookahead, trailing buffer — still rate-limited). No carriage, including the rearmost one, waits behind empty pre-load chunks anymore

#### Chunks Not Unloading When a Train Stops
- Chunks along a train's previous travel direction could remain force-loaded indefinitely after the train stopped, accumulating over a session and degrading performance over time
- Root cause: the anti-thrash "recently loaded" deque only advances when new chunks are loaded; once a train stops, nothing loads, so old lookahead chunks stayed protected from unloading forever
- Fix: the anti-thrash deque is cleared as soon as a train's speed drops below the movement threshold, letting unneeded chunks unload immediately

### Improvements

#### Chunk Loading Tuning
- Adaptive lookahead margin increased from ~2s to ~5s of travel time, to reliably cover cold-terrain chunk generation (which can take 2-3s) — default cap raised from 10 to 20 chunks
- Per-tick chunk load budget reduced to 6 chunks with a 5ms time budget per train, preventing a single train's chunk update from blocking the whole server tick
